meta.titre: Combining sentences with the relative pronouns who and which

sections.contenu_markdown: 'Who' for people, 'which' for things: two sentences about the same subject can always be merged into one with the right relative pronoun.

items: Identifying the repeated noun in two related sentences

sections.contenu_markdown: To combine two sentences sharing the same noun, replace the repeated noun in the second sentence with 'who' (for people) or 'which' (for things), and insert this relative clause directly after the noun it describes in the first sentence.

sections.enonce_markdown: Combine: 'The woman is working in the garden. The woman is my aunt.' (who)

etapes.action: Replace with 'who' in the descriptive clause
etapes.resultat_markdown: who is working in the garden

etapes.action: Insert after the subject of the main sentence
etapes.resultat_markdown: The woman who is working in the garden is my aunt.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The two sentences are merged into one, with the relative clause embedded after the subject.

items.erreur_markdown: Using 'which' for a person instead of 'who'.
items.pourquoi_faux: 'Which' is reserved for things and animals (without personal names), 'who' for people.
items.correction_markdown: Always check whether the repeated noun refers to a person (who) or a thing (which) before combining.

items.enonce_markdown: Combine using 'which': 'The book is on the table. The book is mine.'
items.solution_markdown: The book which is on the table is mine.

items_markdown: The relative clause is inserted right after the noun it describes
